blocks.text: TRL, transformer reinforcement learning, is the Hugging Face library that implements the alignment training methods covered earlier in this course, supervised fine-tuning, DPO, and PPO, as ready to use trainer classes built directly on top of Transformers models.

This topic covers the main trainer classes TRL provides, how each maps to the alignment concepts covered in the Alignment Training module, and how TRL combines with PEFT, covered in the previous topic, for efficient alignment training.
1. TRL Trainer Classes Overview

blocks.alt: SFTTrainer, DPOTrainer, and PPOTrainer are the main TRL trainer classes

blocks.text: TRL provides a family of trainer classes, each implementing a specific training stage covered conceptually earlier in this course, SFTTrainer for supervised fine-tuning, DPOTrainer for direct preference optimization, and PPOTrainer for proximal policy optimization within RLHF, letting each stage be run with a consistent, familiar interface.
2. SFTTrainer for Supervised Fine-Tuning

blocks.alt: A raw dataset goes through SFTTrainer, producing a supervised fine-tuned model

blocks.text: SFTTrainer wraps the standard supervised fine-tuning workflow, covered in an earlier module, handling formatting, packing, and the training loop for instruction or chat style datasets, often the first stage in a full alignment pipeline before any preference optimization stage runs.

code.content:
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    args=SFTConfig(output_dir="./sft-output", max_seq_length=2048),
)
trainer.train()

blocks.text: 3. DPOTrainer for Direct Preference Optimization

blocks.alt: Chosen and rejected pairs go through DPOTrainer, producing an aligned model

blocks.text: DPOTrainer implements DPO, covered in an earlier topic, directly, taking a dataset of chosen and rejected response pairs and optimizing the model toward the chosen responses without needing a separate reward model or reinforcement learning loop.

blocks.text: 4. PPOTrainer for RLHF

blocks.alt: A reward model feeds PPOTrainer, producing an RL tuned model

blocks.text: PPOTrainer implements the reinforcement learning stage of RLHF, covered in earlier topics, taking a trained reward model and using it to drive PPO updates to the policy model, the most involved of the TRL trainers to configure since it requires a working reward model as a prerequisite.

blocks.title: PPOTrainer is generally the hardest TRL trainer to get right
blocks.content: RLHF full pipeline, reward model training followed by PPOTrainer, has more moving parts and more hyperparameters to tune than SFTTrainer or DPOTrainer, consistent with the added complexity of RLHF covered in the earlier comparison topics.

blocks.text: 5. TRL vs PEFT: Different Layers of the Stack

blocks.alt: TRL handles the alignment stage while PEFT is an efficiency technique

blocks.text: TRL and PEFT, covered in the previous topic, solve different problems, TRL provides the training algorithm for a given alignment stage, SFT, DPO, or PPO, PEFT provides a technique for doing that training efficiently with fewer trainable parameters, the two are complementary rather than competing.
6. Combining TRL With PEFT

blocks.alt: A TRL trainer combined with a LoraConfig from PEFT produces efficient alignment training

blocks.text: Every TRL trainer class accepts a PEFT configuration directly, letting an SFT, DPO, or PPO run train only a small set of LoRA adapter parameters instead of the full model, combining the alignment methods covered earlier in this course with the memory efficiency covered in the PEFT and LoRA topics.

code.content:
from peft import LoraConfig
from trl import DPOTrainer, DPOConfig

peft_config = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"])
trainer = DPOTrainer(
    model=model,
    train_dataset=preference_dataset,
    args=DPOConfig(output_dir="./dpo-output"),
    peft_config=peft_config,
)

blocks.text: 7. Why a Dedicated Library Beats a Manual Implementation

blocks.alt: A manual PPO implementation is compared against the TRL PPOTrainer

blocks.text: PPO and DPO both involve subtle implementation details, reference model handling, KL penalty computation, batching for generation, that are easy to get wrong when implemented from scratch, using TRL tested trainer classes avoids re-deriving and re-debugging these details for every project.
8. Where TRL Fits in a Full Pipeline

A typical pipeline using TRL runs SFTTrainer first to establish basic instruction following, then either DPOTrainer or the reward-model-plus-PPOTrainer combination to align the model with preference data, mirroring the staged training approach covered generally in the Alignment Training module.
9. Choosing Which TRL Trainer to Use

The choice among SFTTrainer, DPOTrainer, and PPOTrainer mostly follows the method choice covered in the earlier Preference Optimization synthesis topic, DPOTrainer for paired preference data and simpler training, PPOTrainer when a full RLHF pipeline with a separate reward model is the goal.
Worked Example
A team building an aligned assistant runs SFTTrainer first on a set of instruction examples, producing a model that follows instructions reasonably well but has not yet been tuned on preference data.

They then collect chosen and rejected response pairs and run DPOTrainer, configured with a LoraConfig from PEFT to keep the alignment stage memory efficient, on top of the SFT checkpoint, producing a preference-aligned model without ever needing to train a separate reward model or configure the more involved PPOTrainer.
Common Mistakes

items: Jumping straight to DPOTrainer or PPOTrainer without an SFT stage first, skipping basic instruction following training
Choosing PPOTrainer by default when DPOTrainer would fit the available paired preference data more simply
Not passing a peft_config to a TRL trainer when memory constraints would benefit from parameter-efficient training
Underestimating how many additional moving parts, especially a working reward model, PPOTrainer requires compared to DPOTrainer

blocks.text: Practice

For an alignment training pipeline you are designing, decide which TRL trainer, or sequence of trainers, would fit best given the data you have, chosen and rejected pairs versus a reward model versus raw instruction examples, and justify the choice using the comparisons covered in this topic.
Key Takeaway

TRL provides ready to use trainer classes, SFTTrainer, DPOTrainer, and PPOTrainer, implementing the supervised fine-tuning and alignment methods covered earlier in this course, and combines directly with PEFT configurations to run any of these training stages efficiently, sparing teams from re-implementing the subtle mechanics of DPO or PPO from scratch.
